newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russian GDP up 2 pct in 1998 - Minister.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russian GDP up 2 pct in 1998 - Minister.

text.p: Russia's economy will grow two percent next year and five percent in the year 2000, Economy Minister Yakov Urinson said on Monday.

"We need to get rid of the ballast in every sector more quickly, and then we really will reach two percent growth in GDP in 1998 and five percent in the year 2000," Urinson, also a deputy prime minister, told Ekho Moskvy radio.
Urinson based his forecast of recovery in gross domestic product on current political stability and the fact that output has not fallen for eight months. GDP fell six percent in 1996.
Furthermore companies in every sector were already showing signs of growth, he said.
Earlier central bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said in Basle he hoped Russian GDP would grow two percent this year.
But most ministers have put back their forecasts for the start of recovery to next year from this. Revised budget projections now assume that GDP this year will be flat or down up to two percent.
